Bermuda’s 2021 General Strike: Economic Impact Still Felt Across Sectors

Three years after Bermuda’s landmark general strike that brought the island’s economy to a standstill, business leaders and analysts are reflecting on the lasting effects of that unprecedented industrial action. The 2021 strike, which involved workers from the public and private sectors, halted services ranging from transport and utilities to manufacturing and retail, causing millions of dollars in lost output over the course of its five-day duration.

Among the companies affected was Axalta Coating Systems Ltd, which faced temporary shutdowns at its Pembroke facility. “We experienced significant operational disruption during the strike, with production lines idled and shipments delayed,” said local plant manager Richard DeCosta. “Our team worked overtime in the aftermath to meet customer commitments, but the ripple effects persisted for weeks.”

The Bermuda Chamber of Commerce estimated the direct economic loss from the strike at around $28 million, citing reduced productivity and a sharp dip in consumer spending. “The strike highlighted how interconnected our economy is,” said Chamber President Angela Seymour. “When transport workers walked out, it became almost impossible for other sectors to function normally — even companies not directly involved in the dispute felt the impact.”

The industrial action stemmed from a deadlock over wage increases and job security, with the island’s major unions calling for broad participation. The Bermuda Employers’ Council described the strike as “a wake-up call” for both government and business. “We have since worked closely with unions to improve dialogue and prevent similar disruptions,” said council chair Cecil Darrell.

Tourism, a key pillar of Bermuda’s economy, reportedly suffered losses in bookings and guest nights, while the retail sector faced supply chain bottlenecks. Local analyst Fiona Outerbridge noted, “It took months for some businesses to recover inventory levels and regain customer confidence.”

No significant industrial action has occurred since, but the 2021 strike remains a reference point for labor relations on the island. “It was a challenging period, but it ultimately led to better frameworks for negotiation,” said Bermuda Industrial Union president Marcus Hayward. “Both sides learned valuable lessons.”

Today, Bermuda’s economy is stable, but the memory of 2021’s general strike continues to shape business strategy and labor policy.
